title: Distributed Scanning Strategies to Reduce Electron Beam Damage
content: Electron beam damage limits characterization of a wide variety of materials. Damage arises from a range of mechanisms including radiolysis, knock-on damage, heating, and charging [1, 2]. In insulating materials, charging may induce an E-field strong enough to drive ion diffusion over long length scales outside of the beam [2, 3]. Beam damage is influenced by factors including accelerating voltage, cumulative dose, probe current/dose rate, and probe dwell time [1]. Low-dose experiments suggest permanent damage may result from multiple electrons interacting with the sample while it is in an excited state [4, 5].
